title: GPU Sentinel weekly log - 2027-08-18
body:
GPU Sentinel weekly log — 2027-08-18

Attendees: Ethan Liu (owner), Priya Malhotra, Sofia Ramirez, Marcus O'Neill, Hana Chang (on call), Kevin Patel (SRE async)
Meeting length: 40m standup + 20m dive

Purpose: weekly rollup of regional GPU health signals, short-term capacity moves, and outstanding experiment results. This doc is a working log; action items should be tracked to JIRA tickets (see linked_artifacts).

HIGHLIGHTS / TL;DR:
- EU region sustained higher queue depth during Tuesday surge; added emergency 8-GPU burst capacity from spare-pool for 3 hours, reduced tail latency by ~27%.
- Prewarming experiment v3 (prefix cache warmers) reduced cold-starts for 8k token flows from 19s to 6.5s average in us-west A.
- Observed a subtle regression in APAC auto-scaler: scale-down throttle is firing too early when utilization oscillates, causing oscillation loop. Root cause hypothesized in metric smoothing window (currently 30s).
- Decision: enable model-fallback routing for low-priority batch jobs in EU and APAC for next 48h to reduce pressure on dedicated pools (INFRA-2248).

CURRENT METRICS (past 7 days aggregate, rolling averages):
- Global GPU utilization (serving fleet): 74% avg, 88% peak (local peaks in EU-West on 2027-08-16 15:00 UTC).
- Mean request queue length (global): 12 requests; EU peak 38 during surge window.
- Median 99th percentile token latency (hosted models): 210ms token, tail spiking to 1.1s during preemption events.
- Cold-start rate (models >512M params): 4.8% -> after prewarmer v3 test in us-west A -> 1.6% (delta -3.2pp).
- Preemption rate (spot-style nodes): increased to 0.9% in APAC for the week (baseline 0.3%).

REGIONAL NOTES:
- us-west (primary): prewarmer v3 test completed on 2027-08-17 (run window 02:00-06:00 UTC). Outcome: cold-start reduction consistent across seq-lengths; memory overhead for prewarmer runners ~3.2% CPU. Action: expand prewarmer to an additional 24 nodes (INFRA-2301).

- eu-central: Tuesday surge (09:00-12:30 UTC) caused queue depth >30 for the first time since Q1. Root cause timeline: 1) marketing A/B test drove sustained synchronous bursts, 2) regional autoscaler lag due to delayed metrics from telemetry pipeline (kafka partition lag peaked 40s). Mitigation applied: route low-priority traffic to dedicated fallback pool and spun up spare-pool GPUs. Result: 27% reduction in P95 request time within 20m. Follow-up: add early-warning alert on kafka lag >20s for fleet-telemetry (JIRA created).

- ap-south / southeast-asia: preemption incidents tied to cloud-provider maintenance windows; noted scale-down oscillation in horizontal auto-scaling in ap-south-1. Suggested change: bump smoothing window from 30s to 75s in the HPA controller for those zones, experiment scheduled for 2027-08-20 (canary on 6 pods). Responsible: Priya M.

CAPACITY PLANNING & SHORT-TERM MOVES:
- Spare-pool inventory: 112 GPUs available (mixed A100/T4). Recommend reserving 40 GPUs as a rolling buffer for next 14 days given upcoming marketing event forecast. Proposal doc linked in Confluence.
- Purchase cadence: procurement confirms next tranche of dedicated A100s to start delivery 2027-09-10. Proposal: fast-fail to cloud-bursting for the first week of the campaign if region-level pressure >85% for >30m. Decision needed from product finance by 2027-08-22.
- Cross-region borrow policy: test borrowing cap at 12 GPUs per region to avoid wholesale draining. Ran simulation for 72h: borrowing reduced queue depth on target region by 35% but increased latency for source region by 7%. Recommendation: implement dynamic borrowing with hard cap + priority tiers.

EXPERIMENTS:
- Prewarmer v3 (us-west A): success, expand scope. Notes: prewarmer instances use lightweight kernel cache warming and a tiny prompt set (10 prompts/model). Memory cost predictable.
- Dynamic burst-scaling policy beta: ran across eu-central and us-west small window. Observed unstable behavior when combined with prefix caching; feature flag toggled off for further analysis.
- Eviction-sim for preemption tolerance: synthetic workload showed that keeping KV cache across small preemptions saved ~14% tokens. Need to integrate cache-rehydration hooks in runtime.

RISKS / OPEN QUESTIONS:
- Telemetry lag continues to be a blind spot; kafka to metrics pipeline needs IO tuning. Risk: delayed scaling decisions during surges.
- Procurement timelines still tight relative to a forecasted Q4 campaign; missing arrival would require heavy cloud-bursting and cost delta modeling.
- Preemption oscillation if we increase aggressive scale-down; tightly coupled to HPA thresholds.

DECISIONS MADE THIS WEEK:
- Enable fallback routing for class-B batch jobs in EU/APAC for 48h (owner: Marcus O'Neill, ticket INFRA-2248).
- Expand prewarmer rollout to 24 more nodes in us-west A (owner: Priya Malhotra, ticket INFRA-2301).
- Schedule HPA smoothing window experiment in ap-south on 2027-08-20 (owner: Priya).

ACTION ITEMS (owner — due):
- Marcus O'Neill — create runbook update for fallback routing + rollback steps — due 2027-08-20.
- Priya Malhotra — implement HPA smoothing canary and report results — due 2027-08-22.
- Ethan Liu — coordinate with procurement and finance on burst-vs-buy decision; prepare cost delta spreadsheet — due 2027-08-22.
- Sofia Ramirez — add kafka-lag early-warning alert and link to oncall runbook — due 2027-08-21.
- Hana Chang — perform post-mortem notes for EU surge and capture timeline artifacts — due 2027-08-19.

RUNBOOK / OPERATIONAL NOTES:
- Emergency burst: how-to (short): check spare-pool health dashboard -> allocate GPUs to region via allocate_spare --region <code> --count <n> -> confirm autoscaler accepts new capacity -> notify SRE channel #infra-gpu with tag @oncall. Rolling rollback: deallocate_spare -> ensure queued requests finish - recommended wait 10m.
- Fallback routing toggle: feature flag infra.fallback_routing.{eu,apac} in the console; toggle only after runbook preflight.

NOTES TO FOLLOW-UP IN NEXT WEEK'S LOG:
- Evaluate expanded prewarmer resource footprint across memory-constrained nodes.
- Validate dynamic borrowing cap policy in a longer 7-day simulation.
- Run cost-exposure estimate for cloud-burst scenario for three burst sizes.

Misc quick notes / scratch:
- Observed a pattern: marketing bursts are often weekday mornings in EU; consider shifting some non-critical jobs to off-peak windows.
- Next on-call rotation: Hana -> Marcus starting 2027-08-21.

End of log.

Append final: small housekeeping: rename alert kafka-lag -> fleet.telemetry.kafka_lag_seconds; documented in Confluence page above.
